skill.name: playwriter
skill.description: Control an open Chrome tab with Playwriter to inspect live interfaces, automate browser actions, capture logs, and reproduce frontend issues.
skill.summary: Inspect and debug live Chrome tabs through Playwriter sessions.
skill.author: brianlovin

security_audit.summary: All 19 backtick alerts are Markdown formatting rather than Ruby or shell backtick execution, and the hardcoded URL is a documentation link. Semantic review found high-risk live-tab script access and medium-risk unpinned package execution through npx.

remediation.issue: The skill permits arbitrary scripts and actions in an authenticated browser tab.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before mutation, default to read-only inspection, and restrict evaluate or fetch operations involving sensitive pages.

remediation.issue: The fallback command downloads and executes an unpinned Playwriter package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited package version and avoid automatic installation with npx -y.

static_findings.snippet: 4. Pull logs and structured state via `page.evaluate`.
- If the session attaches to the wrong tab, click the extension icon on the intended tab and re-run
- If `playwriter` command is missing, use `npx -y playwriter ...` or install globally.
Full documentation is available here: https://playwriter.dev/

content.user_title: Debug Live Chrome Tabs with Playwriter
content.value_statement: Frontend issues are difficult to diagnose when they only appear in a user's active browser state. This skill inspects and automates that tab through Playwriter.
actual_capabilities: Attaches Playwriter sessions to an active Chrome tab.
Reads the current page URL, title, and accessibility structure.
Automates targeted clicks, typing, hovering, fetches, and evaluations.
Captures console output and structured page state for debugging.
Inspects list options, popups, and hover content through locators.
limitations: Requires the Playwriter Chrome extension and CLI.
Can attach to the wrong tab if the extension target is incorrect.
Does not launch a separate browser or isolated profile.
Browser actions can expose sensitive data or change live application state.

use_cases.title: Reproduce a Frontend Defect
use_cases.description: Inspect the live page, repeat the failing interaction, and record observed state changes.

use_cases.title: Verify an Interactive Workflow
use_cases.description: Exercise controls in an open application and confirm visible results without launching another browser.

use_cases.title: Collect Browser Evidence
use_cases.description: Capture page structure, console output, and timestamps for a support investigation.

prompt_templates.title: Check the Active Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Attach to the active Chrome tab. Report its URL and title without changing the page.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Page Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Attach to the active tab and collect an accessibility snapshot. Summarize the main controls and visible status messages.

prompt_templates.title: Reproduce a UI Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Reproduce this issue in the active tab: [steps]. Confirm before mutations, capture console output, and report each observed state transition.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Dynamic Application State
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [component] in the active tab. Correlate accessibility data, console messages, and evaluated state, then identify the likely failure point.

output_examples.input: Report the active page URL and title.
output_examples.output: Connected to session 1. The active page is the account settings screen at the reported application URL.

output_examples.input: Inspect the open options list and summarize its state.
output: The list contains six visible options.
No loading or error message is visible.

output_examples.input: Reproduce the save failure and capture evidence.
output_examples.output: The Save action was confirmed before execution. The form remained open, and the console recorded a failed request at the observed timestamp.

best_practices: Confirm the session URL and title before inspecting or changing the page.
Prefer read-only inspection and request confirmation before live mutations.
Redact tokens, personal data, and private content from summaries.
anti_patterns: Do not run arbitrary evaluation code without a defined debugging purpose.
Do not install an unpinned package automatically in a sensitive environment.
Do not perform destructive actions without explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill launch a new browser?
faq.answer: No. It controls a Chrome tab already connected through the Playwriter extension.

faq.question: What must be installed?
faq.answer: The Playwriter Chrome extension must be enabled, and the Playwriter CLI must be available.

faq.question: Can it inspect page structure?
faq.answer: Yes. It can collect accessibility snapshots and inspect elements through Playwriter locators.

faq.question: Can it change the current page?
faq.answer: Yes. It can click, type, hover, fetch, and evaluate scripts when the task requires those actions.

faq.question: How does it avoid using the wrong tab?
faq.answer: Confirm the attached page URL and title before running further commands.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Use read-only inspection when possible and redact tokens, personal data, and private content from every summary.
